# Reading your first results

> When the first run’s answers come back: have them read, then look at the overview, the verdicts, the brands and the sources, in that order, without over-reading.

[← Documentation contents](../README.md) · [Lire cette page en français](../../fr/demarrer/premiers-resultats.md)

The first run gives a snapshot: one answer per prompt and per AI. It is enough to see where the brand appears, who is mentioned instead and which pages are used as sources. It is not enough to talk about a trend. Here is the reading order that gets the most out of a first run.

<a id="wait"></a>

## 1. Wait for the answers to come back

An answer comes back within minutes, 45 at most; Claude’s arrive in a batch within one to two minutes. Meanwhile, the **Prompts** screen shows “answers pending” and updates by itself. The **Collect the answers** button fetches them right away: it is free, only sending is charged. A reading with no answer after 6 hours is marked failed.

<a id="read"></a>

## 2. Have the answers read

To compare the AIs, you need the brands mentioned in each answer, their order and the tone. ChatGPT returns them itself; for the others, a small model reads the text. New answers are read automatically by the background task, which runs every half hour. If the overview shows a banner about answers not read yet, **Read the answers** reads them right away, at the price written next to it (about $0.0008 per answer).

<a id="overview"></a>

## 3. The overview

Read the headline sentence first: the brand appears in so many interface answers out of so many. Then the **Visibility** tile: it only shows from 5 answers, with its margin of error in the help bubble. On a first run, changes read “first measure”: there is nothing to compare.

The **Presence, AI by AI** table tells where the brand is strongest and weakest, and in which form: **Site cited**, **Video cited**, **Name only** or **Read, not cited**. A page read but not cited is the quickest win: it has already been found.

![After the first run, the overview shows visibility by AI and coverage prompt by prompt; the line waits for the second run.](../../../public/docs/captures/en/vue.webp)

*After the first run, the overview shows visibility by AI and coverage prompt by prompt; the line waits for the second run.*

<a id="prompts"></a>

## 4. Verdicts, prompt by prompt

On the **Prompts** screen, each prompt gets a verdict on the interface answers of the period: **Solid** (the brand is in 6 answers out of 10 or more), **Occasional**, **Absent**, or **Too early to tell** below 3 answers. With four interface AIs, a first run gives at most four answers per prompt: the verdict exists, but it is fragile. Start with the **absent** prompts without the brand name: they are the ones where customers discover your competitors.

<a id="brands"></a>

## 5. Who is mentioned instead of you

The **Mentioned instead of us** block of the overview, and the **Competitors** screen, rank the brands the AIs mention on your prompts. Track the ones that matter with **Track**: share of voice and head-to-head fill in, without any new run.

<a id="sources"></a>

## 6. The sources

The **Sources** screen tells which sites and pages the AIs cite, and who gets those citations. Run **Classify the sites** once: each site gets a type (comparison site, media, blog, forum, directory, brand site…), then kept for all projects. That classification orders the work list: a comparison site or a directory where your competitors appear without you comes first.

<a id="act"></a>

## 7. The work list

The **Actions** screen gathers what comes out of this run: your pages found but not cited, other people’s pages to appear on, topics where a video or a page is missing. Each line links to the answers that justify it.

> [!WARNING]
> **What a first run does not tell you**
>
> It does not tell whether the brand is going up or down: that takes at least two run days, and changes are only coloured when they exceed the margin of error. Nor does it tell what a signed-in person sees with their own history: readings start from a neutral session. To settle a specific prompt, use the [deep measurement](../measure/deep-measurement.md).
